title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
summary: Return every node exactly k edges from a target node. Tree edges only point down, so first record each node's parent. Then BFS from the target in three directions (left, right, parent) for k levels.

complexity.note: One pass for parents, one BFS.

intuition: Adding parent links turns the tree into an undirected graph.
BFS level k from the target is exactly the answer.
A visited set stops the BFS from walking back the way it came.
pitfalls: Only searching down from the target misses nodes reached through the parent.
Forgetting the visited set loops between a child and its parent.

title: Path Sum II
summary: Find every root-to-leaf path whose values sum to the target. DFS while keeping the current path and the remaining sum; at a leaf with remaining 0, save a copy of the path. Remove the node from the path when returning.

complexity.note: Copying each found path costs up to O(h).

intuition: Subtract each node's value from the remaining target on the way down.
Only leaves can end a path.
Backtrack: remove the last node from the path after exploring a node.
pitfalls: Saving a path at a non-leaf node whose running sum happens to match.
Pruning when the sum exceeds the target is wrong with negative values.

def pathSum(root: Optional[TreeNode], targetSum: int) -> List[List[int]]:
    res, path = [], []

    def dfs(node: Optional[TreeNode], remain: int) -> None:
        if not node: return
        path.append(node.val)
        remain -= node.val
        if not node.left and not node.right and remain == 0: res.append(path[:])
        dfs(node.left, remain)
        dfs(node.right, remain)
        path.pop()

    dfs(root, targetSum)
    return res

title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
summary: Flatten a tree into a right-leaning list in preorder, in place. For each node with a left child, find the rightmost node of its left subtree, attach the node's right subtree there, then move the left subtree to the right. Continue down the right pointers.

complexity.note: Each edge is walked a constant number of times; no recursion stack.

intuition: In preorder, the right subtree comes right after the last node of the left subtree.
That last node is the rightmost node of the left subtree.
Splice: `rightmost.right = node.right; node.right = node.left; node.left = null`.
pitfalls: Recursive solutions work but use O(h) stack.

title: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
summary: Report nodes column by column, left to right; within a column, top to bottom, and nodes at the same position sorted by value. Give every node a (column, row) coordinate with DFS, then sort all (col, row, value) triples and group by column.
intuition: Root is (col 0, row 0); left child is col − 1, right child is col + 1, both row + 1.
Sort by column, then row, then value: this handles the tie rule.
Group consecutive triples with the same column.
pitfalls: BFS order alone doesn't sort ties at the same position by value.
Confusing this with LeetCode 314, which keeps BFS order for ties.

def verticalTraversal(root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> List[List[int]]:
    nodes = []

    def collect(node: Optional[TreeNode], col: int, row: int) -> None:
        if not node: return
